overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights extreme audience preference for 'What If / Extreme Planetary Conditions' space scenarios and weird cosmological anomalies. Videos focusing on high-concept planetary mechanics (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', A9Qa-RmuOr0 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year', and v1rrcZLdp4U 'The Planet Darker Than Coal') significantly outperform standard biological facts or historical mysteries in both absolute velocity and engagement ratios (likes-per-view).

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) show exceptional early traction and high engagement ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on sensory-rich physics scenarios involving extreme alien worlds where viewers can mentally project themselves into impossible environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring stark paradoxes such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views, 36 likes) drive superior click-through and sustained view velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Pair counter-intuitive temporal or physical extremes (e.g., boiling rain, backward orbits, invisible matter) with fast-paced visual reveals.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content regarding memory trickery and songs stuck in the head (e.g., ef3ND4qiRHc, Jc04LVKNd2s) yields low view counts (<100 views) and near-zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract cognitive psychology tips unless they involve a high-stakes neurological anomaly or bizarre brain-hacking experiment.

weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal facts like octopuses having three hearts (AXAfwrzzEdU) plateau quickly compared to dynamic space scenarios.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal and science content toward extreme survival or bizarre evolutionary anomalies rather than basic textbook trivia.
